title: Comparing things
practiceFocus: Compare two things you know using three structures

points.title: More, less, equal, and the most
points.rule: Más…que and menos…que compare two unequal things. Tan…como compares two equal things. Bueno becomes mejor and malo becomes peor; they do not use más. For a superlative, add el, la, los, or las before más or menos. Keep the adjective agreeing with the noun.

examples.spanish: Mi hermano es más alto que yo.
examples.english: My brother is taller than me.

examples.spanish: Este café es menos caro que ese.
examples.english: This coffee is less expensive than that one.

examples.spanish: Este plato es tan bueno como el otro.
examples.english: This dish is as good as the other one.

examples.spanish: Es el restaurante más caro de la ciudad.
examples.english: It is the most expensive restaurant in the city.

grammar.notYet: Tanto, tanta, tantos, and tantas como for comparing amounts of a noun.

phrases.spanish: Mi ciudad es más tranquila que Madrid.
phrases.english: My city is quieter than Madrid.

phrases.spanish: Este barrio es menos ruidoso que el centro.
phrases.english: This neighbourhood is less noisy than the centre.

phrases.spanish: Ella es tan simpática como su hermana.
phrases.english: She is as nice as her sister.
phrases.note: Reuses simpático and simpática from day 6.

phrases.spanish: Esta comida está tan rica como la de mi madre.
phrases.english: This food is as good as my mother’s.

phrases.spanish: Es el plato más caro del menú.
phrases.english: It is the most expensive dish on the menu.

phrases.spanish: Es la playa más bonita que conozco.
phrases.english: It is the most beautiful beach I know.

phrases.spanish: Mi trabajo es mejor que el anterior.
phrases.english: My job is better than my previous one.
phrases.note: Mejor is irregular. It does not use más.

phrases.spanish: El tráfico hoy es peor que ayer.
phrases.english: The traffic today is worse than yesterday.

phrases.spanish: Mi hermano mayor vive en Barcelona.
phrases.english: My older brother lives in Barcelona.

phrases.spanish: Ella es la menor de la familia.
phrases.english: She is the youngest in the family.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.english: Which restaurant do you prefer, this one or that one?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Este es más barato, pero ese tiene mejor comida.
lines.english: This one is cheaper, but that one has better food.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.spanish: ¿Es tan bueno como el italiano cerca de casa?
lines.english: Is it as good as the Italian place near home?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Creo que sí. Y es menos ruidoso que el italiano.
lines.english: I think so. And it is less noisy than the Italian one.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.spanish: Entonces vamos a este. Es la mejor opción.
lines.english: Then let’s go to this one. It is the best option.

practice.title: Compare two things
practice.instruction: Pick two people, two cities, or two restaurants you know. Compare them using más…que, tan…como, and one superlative with el or la más.
tips: Keep the adjective agreeing with the noun.
That is the same agreement as the job endings on day 3 and the family adjectives on day 6.
